agentCan: Enable the Calendar API, create the client, and declare scopes via Google Cloud APIs
Implement the OAuth flow plus the watch-channel and sync-token machinery (including 410 full-resync handling)
Draft per-scope justifications and the downscope analysis

approval.trigger: Brand verification (prerequisite) plus sensitive-scope verification: per-scope justification and an unlisted YouTube demo video (full grant flow in English, correct app name on the consent screen, client ID visible in the address bar, each scope in use). No security assessment and no annual re-certification for Calendar.
approval.wait: Brand: minutes (automated) to typically 2-3 business days (manual). Sensitive scopes: typically 3-5 business days (both stated by Google)

blockers.detail: Until brand + scope verification complete, users see the unverified-app warning and the project is capped at 100 new users total (platform rules, see the Google guide). Calendar cannot dodge this: reading events is Google's own example of a sensitive scope.
blockers.howToClear: Complete verification before any public launch; stay in Testing mode only for internal pilots.
blockers.title: Unverified until the sensitive-scope review clears

blockers.detail: Push notifications run on watch channels that expire (your requested expiration or Google's internal limit) with NO automatic renewal. You must replace channels with fresh watch calls, run an overlap period, and notification bodies are empty: a ping only says 'something changed', you must call the API to learn what.
blockers.howToClear: Build channel lifecycle management (renewal scheduler + overlap) and treat every ping as a trigger to sync, not as data.
blockers.title: Push channels expire and never auto-renew

blockers.detail: Incremental sync uses syncTokens; when one is invalidated (expiry, ACL changes) the API returns 410 Gone and you must wipe local state and do a full re-sync. Sync tokens are also incompatible with most list filters.
blockers.howToClear: Implement the 410 path as a first-class flow, not an error case.
blockers.title: Sync token invalidation forces full re-sync

sources.label: Sensitive scope verification (3-5 business days; calendar reading example)

tested: Read-only verification: scope list, the sensitive-tier category position, verification requirements, push-channel and sync mechanics were checked against current developers.google.com pages (no project created, nothing submitted)
unverified: Per-scope tier labels for individual Calendar scopes: Google publishes NO per-scope Calendar tier table (unlike Drive and Gmail). The category position (reading events = sensitive) is Google-stated; individual labels, especially for the newer granular scopes (owned, app.created, freebusy, addons), must be confirmed in the console's Data Access page at submission time.
Hands-on time: Google quantifies only waiting times, not active work.
No Calendar equivalent of Gmail's permitted-application-types list was found in the official pages read.

flavor.recommended: A Google Cloud OAuth client (Web application) requesting Calendar API scopes; platform setup is identical to the Google guide
flavor.why: Calendar rides entirely on Google's OAuth platform. What is Calendar-specific is scope choice: Google gives 'reading events stored in Google Calendar' as its own example of a sensitive scope, and no Calendar scope reaches the restricted tier in Google's published material, so verification is the whole game (no CASA, no annual assessment).

humanMust: All Google platform human steps (login/2FA, ToS checkbox, Search Console domain verification, brand publish)
Choose the narrowest scope set against live features
Record the demo video and answer reviewer emails
name: Google Calendar
nuances: Sharing is separately scoped: reading or changing who a calendar is shared with needs the calendar.acls / calendar.acls.readonly scopes; event scopes alone do not cover ACL operations.
Only the same user + same OAuth client that created a push channel can stop it.
Reviewers' own example justification in Google's help pages uses the full calendar scope, so if you request it, expect to defend why narrower scopes cannot work.
Granular scopes are recent additions (events.owned, app.created, events.freebusy); older tutorials that say 'just request calendar' are steering you into the broadest possible ask.
prerequisites: The Google platform setup from the Google guide (Cloud project, branding, verified domain, External audience, OAuth client)
The Calendar API enabled in the project
Your narrowest scope set, mapped to live features

steps.detail: Create the Cloud project, branding, External audience, and OAuth client exactly as in the Google guide, then enable the Calendar API. There is no Calendar-specific console.
steps.title: Set up the Google platform (see Google guide)

steps.detail: Read-only agent: calendar.events.readonly (not calendar.readonly, which also exposes calendar metadata and downloads). Scheduling agent: calendar.events (view/edit events) rather than full calendar (which adds sharing and permanent deletion of calendars themselves). Agent that only manages calendars it creates: calendar.app.created, the tightest write model. Availability-only features: the freebusy scopes expose busy blocks without event contents. Requesting scopes for unimplemented features is prohibited, and reviewers push downscoping by email.
steps.title: Pick the narrowest event scope

steps.detail: Data Access page: declare exactly the scopes your code requests (mismatch triggers the unverified-app screen). Note: Google publishes no per-scope tier table for Calendar; the console groups your declared scopes at submission time and is authoritative.
steps.title: Declare scopes in Data Access

steps.detail: Publish branding, then submit for sensitive-scope verification with per-scope justifications and the demo video (English, full grant flow, consent screen with correct app name, client ID in the address bar, each scope's functionality shown).
steps.time: Prep ~2 hrs; waiting typically 3-5 business days for scopes
steps.title: Submit sensitive-scope verification

steps.detail: If you need realtime updates, build the push machinery properly: watch channels on events/calendarList with your own renewal scheduler (channels expire, no auto-renewal, empty notification bodies), plus incremental sync via syncTokens with a full-resync path on 410 Gone.
steps.title: Implement sync and push correctly

tagline: Same Google platform as Gmail, friendlier ceiling: Calendar scopes top out at the sensitive tier, so verification takes days and there is no security assessment. The craft is choosing the narrowest event scope.

time.active: Platform setup ~1 hr (shared with the Google guide) + ~2 hrs of scope justification and demo video
time.total: About a week, dominated by verification waits
time.waiting: Brand: minutes to 2-3 business days; sensitive scopes: typically 3-5 business days (stated)
